questions.q: In the Microsoft Purview lineage example shown in this lesson, what is the correct order of the chain, left to right?
options: SQL source -> Power BI dataset -> report -> dashboard
Dashboard -> report -> dataset -> SQL source
Report -> dataset -> dashboard -> SQL source
Dataset -> SQL source -> dashboard -> report
questions.explain: The chain reads left to right as data actually flows: the underlying SQL source feeds the dataset, which feeds the report, which feeds the dashboard.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call an executive dashboard 'the tip of a chain most of its viewers never see'?
options: Because the viewer typically only sees the dashboard itself, with no visibility into the source, transformations, dataset, or report behind it
Because dashboards are hidden from executives by default
Because dashboards never contain real data
Because Purview blocks dashboards from being viewed
questions.explain: An executive opening a dashboard sees exactly one box — the rest of the chain (source, dataset, report) is invisible to them unless someone traces it.

questions.q: What does a 'Certified' endorsement badge signal in Power BI, according to this lesson?
options: The content passed a more rigorous review, typically by a central BI or governance team — the strongest trust signal Power BI offers
The content has never been refreshed
The content is scheduled for deletion
The content is only visible to the original creator
questions.explain: Certified is described as the strongest endorsement level, usually set after review by a central governance team, distinct from the lighter 'Promoted' status.

questions.q: What role does Microsoft Purview play relative to Power BI's own lineage view, per this lesson?
options: It scans Power BI tenants and pulls the same lineage into an enterprise-wide catalog alongside other scanned data sources
It replaces Power BI's lineage view entirely and cannot coexist with it
It has no relationship to Power BI lineage at all
It only works for on-premises SQL Server, never Power BI
questions.explain: Purview is an enterprise governance catalog that scans Power BI (among other sources) to surface the same dataset-report-dashboard lineage centrally, at a larger scale than a single workspace.

questions.q: Why do certification/endorsement badges matter even though they aren't a full lineage diagram?
options: Full lineage tracing doesn't scale to every viewer of every dashboard, so badges compress that trust into a single glance
Badges are purely cosmetic and carry no information
Badges automatically fix any upstream data quality issue
Badges replace the need for any lineage tooling entirely
questions.explain: Not every dashboard viewer will or should trace full lineage — badges like Promoted and Certified give a fast trust signal without requiring that effort.
